messages.subject: Baseline Category
parts:
I have a problem that has been going for some time. I do not understand why season.larvae, season.nymphs & season.adult (which are categorical variables for each component of the trivariate model)  reuturn the baseline category in the result output:

season.larvae <- as_factor( season.larvae ) 
season.larvae <- relevel( season.larvae, ref = 2)

season.nymphs <- as_factor( season.nymphs ) 
season.nymphs <- relevel( season.nymphs, ref = 2)

season.adults <- as_factor( season.adults ) 
season.adults <- relevel( season.adults, ref = 2)

This variable has 4 levels; summer = 1, fall = 3, spring = 4 & winter = 2. The code above is trying force inla to set winter = "2" as a reference category but the result, using the "summary()" function return as shown below. Can someone kindly assist in this regard?
---------------

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Baseline Category
parts:
Hi,
This will depend on how you specify the model. E.g. if inla.stack is involved it’s safest to do the conversion to 0/1 variables yourself (with model.matrix) for full control.

I’m also not sure exactly what the ref argument actually does to the factor. If it reorders the levels to put the reference category as 1, it should be fine. If it just sets a flag for which level should be the reference, some code might not know how to deal with that.
I looks from the output that it has reordered the levels, so at least that part should be ok. What’s missing is just the removal of the reference category from the set of 0/1 variables. This is controlled by one of the inla arguments, and I know there can be an issue with that when using inla.stack, but it should otherwise be fine, so more details of your model specification are needed.


Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Baseline Category
parts:
this expansion is coded with std model.matrix call so it should do what
you expect, see attached.

There is always an option to avoid using a reference category but a sum-
to-zero constraint, or even use a overparameterised version (see
?control.fixed and expand.factor.strategy)
